dependencyDashboard.header:
This issue lists Renovate updates and detected dependencies; the [Dependency Dashboard](https://docs.renovatebot.com/key-concepts/dashboard/) docs explain the layout.

**How we use Renovate**

- Updates are raised before 6am UTC on Saturday, Sunday and Monday. Security fixes are raised at any time and are never automerged.
- Minor, patch and digest updates automerge once CI passes for GitHub Actions, pre-commit hooks, the compose test images and dev-only dependencies.
- Major updates, runtime dependencies, the Postgres image, the Python and Node versions and lock file maintenance need a manual review.
- Each rule in `.github/renovate.json` has a `description` that says why it exists.
dependencyDashboard.footer: To check that a rule matches, see "Renovate" in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/samcorky/menagerist/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

packageRules.description: Dashboard headings, one per area of the repository. They only change how the Dependency Dashboard is laid out, not which updates share a pull request (groupName does that). Rules further down override these for the language runtimes
Dashboard heading for the frontend
Dashboard heading for CI and tooling
Dashboard heading for Docker images and compose files

filetype is a small, finished file-signature library with no releases since 2022; exempt it from the abandonment warning. The manager is pep621; its datasource is pypi, which an earlier version of this rule had wrong
Tell the two lock file maintenance pull requests apart (they share a title otherwise)
Tell the two lock file maintenance pull requests apart (they share a title otherwise)
Our own image is not a dependency to track: compose.yaml ships `latest` on purpose (a digest would freeze every new install on one build), and the compose.smoke.yaml tag is built locally

The proxy harness images float on purpose: it exists to notice when a new nginx, Caddy or Traefik release changes how an early upload reply is relayed, so a digest pin would freeze it and add a weekly digest pull request for test-only images

Automerge minor, patch and digest bumps of the compose images (the proxy harness, e2e and smoke stacks). Listed before the Postgres rule, which turns automerge back off for the shipped database image, and before the major rule, which does the same for majors
One Postgres bump updates compose.yaml and backend/tests/conftest.py together. No digest pin: the CI image cache is keyed on the compose.yaml name and the tests ask for the tag
Group all Python interpreter version bumps (.python-version and the requires-python floors) into one PR, and treat as a major/manual-review change
Group Python runtime dependencies (project.dependencies)
Group Python dev/tooling dependencies (dependency-groups.dev and release)
Group Python build-system requirements (build-system.requires)
TypeScript 7 is outside the peer range of SvelteKit 2 (typescript ^5.3.3 || ^6.0.0); remove once SvelteKit supports it
SvelteKit 3 cannot install while bits-ui depends on runed 0.35 (peer @sveltejs/kit ^2.21.0); the adapter must match SvelteKit. Remove once bits-ui moves to a runed that accepts SvelteKit 3
Frontend (npm) updates are grouped by how they fail, not all together, so one bad release blocks only its own group. Later rules override this catch-all; each major update gets its own pull request
The Svelte toolchain is coupled by peer ranges, so it moves in one pull request, majors included

vitest and its coverage provider pin each other's exact version through peer ranges, so they move in one pull request. The Svelte toolchain rule's old /^vite/ pattern matched vitest too, which pulled it into that group and left @vitest/coverage-v8 alone, a combination npm could not resolve
Lint and format tooling only affects lint results, so its minor and patch updates automerge once CI passes
UI libraries change what users see and are where e2e regressions come from
bits-ui gets its own pull request: 2.20 fails advanced-search.spec.ts:166 and field-types.spec.ts:209, and it holds back SvelteKit 3, so it should not block the other UI libraries
Runtime npm dependencies ship to users and need a manual review; keeping them in their own group lets the dev-only groups above automerge instead of one runtime package making the whole group manual
Group GitHub Actions updates together and pin SHA digests
Automerge GitHub Actions updates
Group pre-commit hook updates together
Automerge pre-commit hook updates
Automerge non-major devDependency and lint/format tooling updates
Require manual review for all major updates
Require manual review for runtime/production dependencies
One pull request pins all npm packages (otherwise there are several, all titled Pin dependencies)
One pull request pins the Docker images by digest
hatchling, hatch-vcs and calver-scm are pinned in build-system.requires and in a dependency group; keep both in one pull request so they move together
Workflow and composite action updates are CI changes
Docker images and the Python build system are build changes
Build-system requirements (hatchling, hatch-vcs, calver-scm) are build changes

Group Node version bumps (.node-version, which CI and the Dockerfile read, the engines.node range in frontend/package.json, the Renovate tool constraint and the @types/node typings) into one PR, and treat as a major/manual-review change. Matched by package name alone, because the tool constraint comes from no single manager, and kept last because a later rule would override its group (the npm catch-all and the major rule both do). separateMultipleMajor is off because the npm catch-all turns it on, which split these into one pull request per major
